::: {.why}
Tree-based importance is biased toward high-cardinality and correlated features in ways that have nothing to do with predictive value, and the fix is a permutation test you already know how to run.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say why impurity-based importance is misleading here and what permutation importance measures instead.
- Report permutation importance with a null distribution and identify which features are indistinguishable from noise.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement permutation importance correctly for this setting: permute a feature within each cross-section rather than globally, so you break its relationship to the label without destroying the cross-sectional structure. Then repeat many times to get a null distribution per feature, not a point estimate.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Handle the correlated-feature problem: permuting one of two correlated features leaves the model able to use the other, so both look unimportant. Run grouped permutation for correlated clusters and report both the individual and the grouped results, since the difference is itself informative.
:::
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Why is tree-based feature importance misleading here, and what does grouped permutation tell you that individual permutation does not?
